title: Finite codimension-at-most-one points on an integral separated scheme have a common affine neighbourhood
statement: Let $X$ be an integral separated scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Let $T\subseteq X$ be a finite set of points, possibly empty. Suppose that for every $x\in T$ the local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and has Krull dimension at most one [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Then there exists an affine open subscheme $V\subseteq X$ containing $T$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum].

source.place: Tag 09NJ (lemma-finite-set-codim-1-points-in-affine), statement; used in Tag 09NN (proposition-finite-set-of-points-of-codim-1-in-affine), proof, last sentence: the integral case.

proof.text: Write $\eta$ for the generic point and $K=\mathcal O_{X,\eta}$. By [lem-sc-integral-scheme-stalks-in-function-field], every $A_x=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ embeds in $K$ with fraction field $K$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism], the image of $\operatorname{Spec}(A_x)\to X$ contains every generalization of $x$, including $\eta$. If $\dim A_x=0$, the domain $A_x$ has only its zero prime: any other prime would give a strict prime chain of length one. Since its maximal ideal is a prime, it is zero, so $A_x$ is a field and its spectrum is a singleton. Its image contains both $x$ and $\eta$, hence $x=\eta$. Remove $\eta$ from the finite set and enumerate the remaining distinct points $x_1,\ldots,x_r$. Their local rings have dimension exactly one. If $r=0$, choose any point of the nonempty integral scheme $X$ and an affine neighbourhood using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]; it contains $\eta$ because every nonempty open does. This proves the assertion for $T=\varnothing$ and $T\subseteq\{\eta\}$. Henceforth $r\geq1$.

source.place: Tag 09NJ, opening sentence, with explicit reduction of the dimension-zero and empty cases.

proof.text: Put $A_i=\mathcal O_{X,x_i}\subset K$. There is no discrete valuation subring $\mathcal O\subset K$ containing both $A_i$ and $A_j$ for $i\ne j$. Indeed, the contraction to $A_i$ of the maximal ideal of $\mathcal O$ is either zero or the maximal ideal of $A_i$, since $A_i$ is a one-dimensional local domain. In the zero case every nonzero element of $A_i$ is a unit of $\mathcal O$, so $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A_i)\subseteq\mathcal O$, contrary to a discrete valuation ring being a nonfield. Thus the inclusion $A_i\to\mathcal O$ is local, and likewise for $A_j$. Compose the two spectrum maps with the canonical morphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism]. The resulting maps $\operatorname{Spec}(\mathcal O)\to X$ agree on $\operatorname{Spec}(K)$, where both are the canonical generic-point map, by the stalk embeddings in Step 1. Uniqueness for the separated structure morphism, [lemma-nagata-separated-valuation-lift-unique], makes them equal. The closed point then maps both to $x_i$ and to $x_j$, contradicting their distinctness.

source.place: Tag 09NJ, proof, first paragraph and displayed valuative diagram; Schemes Tag 01KZ (schemes-lemma-separated-implies-valuative).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-one-dimensional-subrings-common-dvr-criterion] to $A_i,A_j\subset K$. Its Noetherian and dimension-one hypotheses hold by the original assumptions and Step 1. Step 2 excludes its common-DVR alternative, so $A_i\otimes_{\mathbb Z}A_j\to K$ is surjective for every $i\ne j$.

Apply [lem-trf-semilocal-subring-affine-gluing] to the nonempty finite family $A_1,\ldots,A_r$. Every $A_i$ is local, hence semilocal; the other hypotheses are Step 1 and Step 3. Obtain a domain $A\subset K$ with fraction field $K$, an open covering of $S=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ by $S_i=\operatorname{Spec}(A_i)$, and distinct closed points $m_i$ with $A_{m_i}=A_i$. For $i\ne j$ the overlaps are $\operatorname{Spec}(K)$ with the maps prescribed by the inclusions in $K$.

source.place: Tag 09NJ, proof, application of Tag 09N4 and displayed open covering.

proof.text: Let $c_i:S_i\to X$ be the canonical local-ring morphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism]. On every overlap $S_i\cap S_j=\operatorname{Spec}(K)$ their restrictions are the canonical map at $\eta$: in an affine neighbourhood of $x_i$ the map is induced by taking germs, and localizing further to the zero prime gives the germ at $\eta$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] gives $f:S\to X$ restricting to $c_i$. The closed point $m_i$ maps to $x_i$. The induced map on local rings at $m_i$ is an isomorphism, since restricting to the open chart $S_i$ identifies it with the closed-point stalk map of $c_i$, which is the identity of $A_i$. Also $S$ has the single generic point $(0)$, whose image is $\eta$, since this holds on each chart. Hence the map between the generic-point sets is a bijection of singletons.

source.place: Tag 09NJ, proof, gluing the canonical morphisms and matching local rings.

proof.text: By [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated], $X$ is quasi-separated. It has exactly one irreducible component, since it is integral. Apply [lem-trf-affine-source-stalk-isomorphism-neighbourhood] to $f:S\to X$ and $m_1,\ldots,m_r$. Its affine-source hypothesis holds because $S=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$; its finite and injective generic-point hypotheses and its stalk-isomorphism hypotheses were checked in Step 5. Obtain an affine open $V$ containing all $x_i$. It is nonempty, so it also contains $\eta$. This restores any removed generic point and gives $T\subseteq V$.

source.place: Tag 09NJ, proof, final sentence applying Tag 09NI.

proof_origin.place: Tag 09NJ (varieties-lemma-finite-set-codim-1-points-in-affine), full proof; empty/generic-point cases and the local nature of inclusions in a common DVR expanded explicitly.
